title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is printed upside down. It is not Grothendieck's own manuscript: it is a typed English page, numbered III.5, from what looks like a thesis or preprint on separable (Azumaya) algebras over a ringed space (X, 𝔄). Grothendieck evidently used its back for his French notes on motives and Hodge/effectivity structures, which are the surrounding pages. Its mathematics is unrelated to those notes.

(1) Lines 1–4 end the proof of a lemma. Write W = End_A(M) for M finitely generated projective and faithful, and W^e for its enveloping algebra. M ⊗_A Hom_A(M,A) is projective as a left W^e-module. The map μ is a W^e-isomorphism (essentially W ≅ M ⊗ M*). Hence W is W^e-projective, i.e. separable over A.

(2) Theorem III.4: if 𝔐 is a faithful, locally projective sheaf of finite type over 𝔄, then the sheaf Hom_𝔄(𝔐,𝔐) is a locally separable (Azumaya) 𝔄-algebra. The proof runs:
- By Theorem II.2, Ω = Hom_𝔄(𝔐,𝔐) is locally projective of finite type.
- Finite presentation gives that stalks of Hom are Hom of stalks.
- Each stalk End(𝔐_x) is central separable over 𝔄_x.
- Theorem III.2, a stalkwise criterion, then concludes.

(3) Theorem III.5: the tensor product of two locally separable 𝔄-algebras is locally separable. The proof notes that stalks commute with ⊗. It cites Auslander–Goldman, 'The Brauer group of a commutative ring' (1960), Prop. 1.5, for central separability of a tensor product of central separable algebras. It then applies Theorem III.2 again.

This is the sheafified Azumaya-algebra theory underlying a Brauer group of a ringed space or scheme, i.e. that group's closure under ⊗ and its trivial class End(E).
errors: Theorem III.5's proof checks only the stalk condition. Theorem III.2 presumably also needs 𝓛1 ⊗ 𝓛2 to be locally projective of finite type. That follows easily from the same property for each factor, but it is not stated: a minor gap in exposition.

ideas.what: The endomorphism sheaf of a faithful locally projective module of finite type is an Azumaya algebra.
ideas.modern_name: Azumaya algebra End(E), the trivial class in the Brauer group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Azumaya (1951), Auslander–Goldman (1960); for sheaves/schemes, Grothendieck 'Le groupe de Brauer I' (1966)
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas)

ideas.what: Tensor product of Azumaya algebras over a ringed space is Azumaya, checked stalkwise.
ideas.modern_name: Brauer group closed under tensor product

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of someone else's routine exposition of Azumaya algebras over a ringed space, reused as scrap paper. Its content is standard Auslander–Goldman / Grothendieck Brauer-group material and unrelated to the motivic notes on the neighbouring pages.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. The text is a typescript in English, not Grothendieck's handwriting; script letters 𝔐 and 𝔄 are filled in by hand.
In Theorem III.4's statement, the sheaf Hom is underlined as Hom_𝔄(𝔐,𝔐).
The 'μ' in line 2 is the handwritten Greek letter μ, as transcribed.
